The **2012 Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council election** was held on **3 May 2012**, as part of the **2012 United Kingdom local elections**. One-third of the council's seats (21 out of 63) were up for election, with each successful candidate serving a four-year term.

### **Background**
- **Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council** is the local authority for the Metropolitan Borough of Stockport in Greater Manchester, England.
- The council was under **no overall control (NOC)** before the election, with the **Liberal Democrats** as the largest party but without a majority.
- The election took place alongside other local elections across England, Scotland, and Wales, as well as the **London mayoral and assembly elections**.

---

### **Political Context**
- The **Conservative-Liberal Democrat coalition** was in power nationally (since 2010), which may have influenced local voting patterns.
- The **Labour Party** was performing well in opinion polls nationally, benefiting from dissatisfaction with austerity measures.
- Stockport had been a **Liberal Democrat stronghold** for many years, but Labour was making gains in urban areas.

---

### **Results Summary**
| **Party**       | **Seats Contested (2012)** | **Seats Won (2012)** | **Net Change** | **Total Seats (After 2012)** |
|-----------------|---------------------------|---------------------|----------------|-----------------------------|
| **Labour**      | 21                        | 15                  | **+6**         | **26**                      |
| **Lib Dem**     | 21                        | 4                   | **-7**         | **20**                      |
| **Conservative**| 19                        | 2                   | **-1**         | **15**                      |
| **Green**       | 5                         | 0                   | **0**          | **1**                       |
| **UKIP**        | 3                         | 0                   | **0**          | **0**                       |
| **Independent** | 1                         | 0                   | **0**          | **1**                       |

#### **Key Outcomes:**
- **Labour gained 6 seats**, becoming the **largest party** on the council (26 seats).
- The **Liberal Democrats lost 7 seats**, falling to **20 seats** (their worst result in Stockport in years).
- The **Conservatives lost 1 seat**, dropping to **15 seats**.
- The **Green Party** (which had 1 seat before the election) and **UKIP** (standing for the first time in Stockport) **won no seats**.
- **Turnout** was **32.6%**, slightly lower than the **35.6%** in the 2011 election.

---

### **Ward-Level Results**
Labour made gains in several key wards, particularly in more urban and working-class areas, while the Liberal Democrats held on in more affluent suburbs.

| **Ward**            | **2012 Winner** | **Previous Holder (2008)** | **Change?** |
|---------------------|----------------|---------------------------|-------------|
| **Brinnington & Central** | Labour | Labour | Hold |
| **Bredbury & Woodley** | Labour | Lib Dem | **Lab Gain** |
| **Bredbury Green & Romiley** | Lib Dem | Lib Dem | Hold |
| **Cheadle & Gatley** | Lib Dem | Lib Dem | Hold |
| **Cheadle Hulme North** | Lib Dem | Lib Dem | Hold |
| **Cheadle Hulme South** | Lib Dem | Lib Dem | Hold |
| **Davenport & Cale Green** | Labour | Lib Dem | **Lab Gain** |
| **Edgeley & Cheadle Heath** | Labour | Labour | Hold |
| **Hazel Grove** | Lib Dem | Lib Dem | Hold |
| **Heald Green** | Lib Dem | Lib Dem | Hold |
| **Heatons North** | Labour | Lib Dem | **Lab Gain** |
| **Heatons South** | Labour | Lib Dem | **Lab Gain** |
| **Manor** | Labour | Labour | Hold |
| **Marple North** | Conservative | Conservative | Hold |
| **Marple South** | Conservative | Conservative | Hold |
| **Offerton** | Labour | Lib Dem | **Lab Gain** |
| **Reddish North** | Labour | Labour | Hold |
| **Reddish South** | Labour | Labour | Hold |
| **Stepping Hill** | Lib Dem | Lib Dem | Hold |
| **St Mary’s (Stockport town centre)** | Labour | Lib Dem | **Lab Gain** |
| **Woodley** | Labour | Lib Dem | **Lab Gain** |

#### **Notable Gains:**
- Labour took **Bredbury & Woodley**, **Davenport & Cale Green**, **Heatons North**, **Heatons South**, **Offerton**, **St Mary’s**, and **Woodley** from the Liberal Democrats.
- The **Conservatives held** their two seats in **Marple North** and **Marple South** but lost ground elsewhere.

---

### **Aftermath & Council Composition**
- After the election, the council remained under **no overall control**, but Labour was the largest party.
- The **Liberal Democrats** (20 seats) and **Conservatives** (15 seats) could no longer form a majority together (they had 35 vs. Labour’s 26).
- A **Labour-Liberal Democrat coalition** was discussed, but no formal agreement was reached.
- The **Green Party** retained their single seat (held by **Sue Coe** in **Davenport & Cale Green** until 2014).
- The **Independent** councillor was **Walter Brett**, who had left the Liberal Democrats in 2011.

---

### **National & Local Trends**
- The **2012 local elections** were a **disaster for the Liberal Democrats**, who lost over **300 seats nationwide** due to their role in the coalition government.
- **Labour made significant gains** across the North West, including in **Manchester**, **Salford**, and **Tameside**.
- **UKIP** performed poorly in Stockport but would later gain traction in the **2014 European elections**.

---

### **Subsequent Elections**
- In **2014**, Labour **gained further seats**, becoming the **largest party** with **30 seats** (still short of a majority).
- The **Liberal Democrats collapsed further**, falling to **13 seats** by **2016**.
- By **2018**, Labour had **33 seats**, forming a **minority administration** (the first Labour-led council in Stockport since the 1970s).

---

### **Key Figures in 2012**
- **Sue Derbyshire** (Labour) – Later became **Leader of Stockport Council** (2016–2023).
- **Iain Roberts** (Lib Dem) – Former council leader (2005–2011).
- **Colin Foster** (Conservative) – Opposition leader at the time.

---
### **Sources & Further Reading**
- [Stockport Council Election Results (2012)](https://www.stockport.gov.uk/elections)
- [BBC News – 2012 Local Elections](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-17942695)
- [The Guardian – Local Election Results (2012)](https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2012/may/04/local-elections-2012-results)
- [Manchester Evening News – Stockport Election Coverage](https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/)
